mainTopic: בן זומא and the upper and lower waters, and how אחר (אלישע בן אבויה) left the Torah and refused רבי מאיר's pleas to return
overview: The amud opens in the middle of a question to בן זומא: may a pregnant woman who still seems to be a בתולה marry a כהן גדול? He answers that שמואל's rare case does not matter, but she may have conceived in a bath. The גמרא defends that answer against another statement of שמואל. Next, a ברייתא tells how רבי יהושע found בן זומא lost in thought about the gap between the upper and lower waters, and said he was 'still outside.' The גמרא shows the flaw in בן זומא's proof and lists opinions on how wide that gap is. Then the גמרא turns to אחר, אלישע בן אבויה. He saw the angel מיטטרון sitting in heaven, wrongly thought there might be two powers, heard a בת קול shut him out from תשובה, and left the Torah. Several stories follow in which his student רבי מאיר keeps begging him to return, and אחר keeps answering that the heavenly voice excluded him. The amud ends as רבי מאיר brings him from one place of learning to another to hear children's verses, and the story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Should we worry about שמואל's rare ability?
steps.stepSummary: The question to בן זומא ends: should we worry that she lost her virginity without bleeding, as שמואל could do, or is that too rare to matter?
steps.simpleTranslation: [שמואל said:] 'I can have relations several times without blood.' Or perhaps a case like שמואל's is not common?
steps.whatsHappening: The text picks up in the middle of a question asked to בן זומא about a pregnant woman who still seems to be a בתולה. The question is whether to worry about שמואל's rare case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If relations without bleeding are possible, this woman may really have had relations and would be forbidden to a כהן גדול, who must marry a בתולה. The other side of the question is that such a case is unusual, and the law does not worry about unusual cases.

phrases.english: I am able to have relations
phrases.notes: These are שמואל's own words, quoted as part of the question to בן זומא.

phrases.english: several times without blood.
Or perhaps a case like שמואל's is not common?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the question to בן זומא that began before this section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Must we worry about שמואל's rare case when judging whether a pregnant בתולה is permitted to a כהן גדול?

steps.title: בן זומא: שמואל's case is rare, but she may have conceived in a bath
steps.stepSummary: בן זומא answers that we ignore שמואל's rare case, but we do worry that she became pregnant in a bath.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: שמואל's case is not common, and we are concerned that she became pregnant in a bath.
steps.whatsHappening: בן זומא answers. He sets aside שמואל's case as too rare, and offers another way she could be pregnant while still a בתולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the pregnancy itself does not prove she had relations. She could have bathed in water that held a man's seed and conceived that way, so she can stay a בתולה and remain permitted to a כהן גדול.

keyTerms.meaning: we are concerned / we take into account

steps.whatToRemember: A pregnant woman who still seems to be a בתולה may have conceived in a bath, so she is not assumed to have had relations.

phrases.english: He said to them: a case like שמואל's is not common,
and we are concerned that perhaps she became pregnant in a bath.
phrases.notes: He means she bathed in water that had a man's seed in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמואל's case is too rare to matter, but conception in a bath is a real possibility.

steps.title: Challenge: שמואל says seed must shoot like an arrow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the bath idea: שמואל taught that seed not released with force cannot cause pregnancy.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't שמואל say: any seed that does not shoot out like an arrow cannot cause pregnancy!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks בן זומא's answer, using another statement of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Seed floating in bathwater does not shoot like an arrow. According to שמואל, then, it could not cause pregnancy, and the bath explanation seems impossible.

phrases.english: But didn't שמואל say: any seed
that does not shoot like an arrow cannot cause pregnancy!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: בן זומא's claim that she may have conceived in a bath.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Seed in a bath is not released with force, and שמואל says such seed cannot cause pregnancy.

steps.title: Answer: it shot like an arrow at the start
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the seed was released with force at first, and that is enough even if pregnancy happens later.
steps.simpleTranslation: At the start, too, it shot like an arrow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the bath explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's rule only requires that the seed was released with force when it first left the man. It does not need to shoot like an arrow at the moment of pregnancy, so seed in a bath can still qualify.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's rule is met if the seed shot like an arrow when it was first released, even if pregnancy happens later.

phrases.english: At the start it also shot like an arrow.
phrases.notes: When it first left the man, it shot out with force, and that is enough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the meaning of the cited rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Seed must shoot like an arrow at the moment of pregnancy.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is enough that it shot like an arrow when first released.

steps.title: The story: בן זומא does not stand for רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells how בן זומא, lost in thought, did not stand up for רבי יהושע בן חנניה, who asked him what was on his mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Once רבי יהושע בן חנניה was standing on a step on the הר הבית. בן זומא saw him and did not stand up before him. He said to him: From where and to where, בן זומא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story about בן זומא. This step sets the scene for the conversation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Standing for one's teacher is expected, so failing to stand shows that בן זומא was deeply absorbed in thought. רבי יהושע's question 'from where and to where' means 'what are you thinking about?'

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן חֲנַנְיָה
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: There was an incident with Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananya

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיָה עוֹמֵד עַל גַּב מַעֲלָה בְּהַר הַבַּיִת,
phrases.english: who was standing on a step on the Temple Mount,

phrases.aramaic: וְרָאָהוּ בֶּן זוֹמָא וְלֹא עָמַד מִלְּפָנָיו.
phrases.english: and ben Zoma saw him and did not stand up before him.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: מֵאַיִן וּלְאַיִן בֶּן זוֹמָא?
phrases.english: He said to him: From where and to where, ben Zoma?
phrases.notes: He's asking: where is your mind right now?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן חֲנַנְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new story about בן זומא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets the scene: בן זומא was so absorbed in thought that he did not stand for his teacher.

steps.title: בן זומא: only three fingers between the upper and lower waters
steps.stepSummary: בן זומא says he was thinking about the gap between the upper and lower waters, which he says is only three fingers wide, proving it from a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I was gazing between the upper waters and the lower waters, and there are only three fingers between them, as it says: 'And the spirit of God hovered over the face of the waters,' like a dove hovering over its young without touching them.
steps.whatsHappening: בן זומא answers רבי יהושע's question and explains what he was thinking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the word 'hovered' (מרחפת) like a dove hovering over its chicks: very close, but not touching. From that he concludes the two sets of waters are separated by only a tiny gap.

phrases.english: He said to him: I was gazing
between the upper waters and the lower waters,
and there is nothing between this and that
except a mere three fingers,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְרוּחַ אֱלֹהִים מְרַחֶפֶת עַל פְּנֵי הַמָּיִם״ —
phrases.english: as it is stated: "And the spirit of God hovered over the face of the waters"
phrases.notes: בראשית 1:2

phrases.aramaic: כְּיוֹנָה שֶׁמְּרַחֶפֶת עַל בָּנֶיהָ וְאֵינָהּ נוֹגַעַת.
phrases.english: like a dove that hovers over its young and does not touch them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יהושע's question in step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He was thinking about the gap between the upper and lower waters, only three fingers wide, as shown by 'hovered.'

steps.title: רבי יהושע: בן זומא is still outside
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע tells his students that בן זומא has not yet fully grasped these matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to his students: בן זומא is still outside.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע gives his verdict on what בן זומא said, and the story ends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Still outside' means בן זומא had not truly entered the inner understanding of these deep matters. The next step explains what was wrong with his reasoning.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע judged that בן זומא had not yet properly understood these deep matters.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to his students:
Ben Zoma is still outside.
phrases.notes: He means בן זומא has not yet fully understood these matters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יהושע's verdict on בן זומא's words.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: בן זומא's understanding of the waters of creation was incomplete.

steps.title: Why the proof fails: the hovering came before the separation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows the flaw in בן זומא's proof: the hovering פסוק is about Day One, but the waters were only separated on Day Two.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, 'And the spirit of God hovered over the face of the waters,' when was that? On the first day. The separation happened on the second day, as it says: 'And let it divide between waters and waters.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יהושע said בן זומא was 'outside,' by pointing out a flaw in his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the first day there were not yet upper and lower waters at all. A פסוק about Day One cannot teach the size of a gap that only came into being on Day Two.

keyTerms.meaning: now, consider (introduces a point both sides accept)

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּדֵי ״וְרוּחַ אֱלֹהִים מְרַחֶפֶת עַל פְּנֵי הַמָּיִם״
phrases.english: Now, "And the spirit of God hovered over the face of the waters"
when was it? On the first day,
while the separation happened on the second day,
as it is written: "And let it divide between waters and waters."
phrases.notes: בראשית 1:6

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדֵי ״וְרוּחַ אֱלֹהִים מְרַחֶפֶת עַל פְּנֵי הַמָּיִם״ אֵימַת הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains רבי יהושע's verdict by attacking בן זומא's proof.
steps.kashyaTarget: בן זומא's proof from 'hovered' about the gap between the upper and lower waters.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The hovering happened on Day One, before the waters were divided on Day Two, so it cannot describe the gap between them.

steps.title: How big is the gap?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how big the gap between the upper and lower waters really is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that בן זומא's proof was rejected, the גמרא asks what the real size of the gap is. This sets up the opinions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumes there is a gap, and that it is small. It only asks how small.

phrases.english: And how much?
phrases.notes: How wide is the gap between the upper and lower waters?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting בן זומא's measure, asks for the true size of the gap.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The actual size of the gap between the upper and lower waters.

steps.title: A hair's width, or like bridge boards
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב says the gap is the width of a hair; the רבנן say it is like the gap between the boards of a bridge.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: like the full width of a hair. And the רבנן say: like the boards of a bridge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first two answers to the question of how big the gap is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions picture a very thin gap, the kind of space between two things that lie right next to each other. They differ only in which image best shows how narrow it is.

keyTerms.meaning: the full width of a hair or thread

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: כִּמְלֹא נִימָא.
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov said: like the full width of a hair.
And the Rabbis say: like the boards of a bridge.
phrases.notes: Picture the thin gap between boards laid next to each other on a bridge.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: כִּמְלֹא נִימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The gap is as thin as a hair, or like the gap between bridge boards.

steps.title: Two robes spread over each other, or two cups
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא (or רב אסי) compares the gap to two robes spread one on the other; another version compares it to two cups placed one on the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא, and some say רב אסי, said: like two robes spread one over the other. And some say: like two cups placed one upon the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds more opinions on the size of the gap, ending the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each picture shows two layers lying almost on top of each other with only a tiny space between. The point is that the upper and lower waters are extremely close but do not touch.
steps.whatToRemember: The upper and lower waters are very close but not touching. The opinions differ only on how small the gap is: a hair, bridge boards, two robes, or two cups.

phrases.aramaic: מָר זוּטְרָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב אַסִּי אָמַר:
phrases.english: Mar Zutra, and some say Rav Asi, said:
like two robes spread one over the other.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ: כִּתְרֵי כָסֵי דִּסְחִיפִי אַהֲדָדֵי.
phrases.english: And some say: like two cups placed one upon the other.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר זוּטְרָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב אַסִּי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more answers to the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The gap is like that between two robes or two cups laid one upon the other.

steps.title: אחר cut down the saplings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to אחר from the four who entered the פרדס and attaches a פסוק from קהלת to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: אחר cut down the saplings. About him the פסוק says: 'Do not let your mouth bring your flesh into sin.'
steps.whatsHappening: After the side discussion about בן זומא and the waters, the גמרא now turns to the third person who entered the פרדס, אחר. It sets up the next question: what exactly did he do?
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Cut down the saplings' is a picture of going off the path into heresy. The פסוק warns that words and thoughts can bring a person to sin, which hints that אחר's downfall started with a mistaken thought.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'the other one.' This is the name given to אֱלִישָׁע בֶּן אֲבוּיָה after he left the Torah.
Cut down the saplings, a picture of becoming a heretic.

steps.confusionAlert: 'Cutting saplings' here is not about gardening. It is a picture of going astray in matters of faith.

phrases.english: Acher cut down the saplings,
phrases.notes: This picks up the earlier story of the four who entered the 'orchard,' the פרדס.

phrases.english: about him the verse says:
"Do not let your mouth
bring your flesh into sin."
phrases.notes: קהלת 5:5

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the בן זומא discussion and returns to the list of the four who entered the פרדס.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אחר became a heretic, and the פסוק about the mouth causing the flesh to sin applies to him.

steps.title: What happened to אחר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what event led אחר to heresy.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what actually happened to אחר. It is setting up the story that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 only said that he went astray. Now the גמרא wants the cause.

keyTerms.meaning: What was it? A request for the story behind a statement.

phrases.english: What was it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the details behind step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What event caused אחר to 'cut down the saplings.'

steps.title: אחר sees מיטטרון sitting and draws a wrong conclusion
steps.stepSummary: אחר saw the angel מיטטרון sitting and writing Israel's merits. Since he knew there is no sitting above, he wondered whether there are two powers.
steps.simpleTranslation: He saw מיטטרון, who had been given permission to sit and write the merits of Israel. He said: We have a tradition that above there is no sitting, no competition, no turning one's back, and no tiredness. Perhaps, Heaven forbid, there are two powers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: אחר saw an angel sitting in heaven. That clashed with a tradition he knew, so he came to a terrible conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sitting is a sign of authority, and he had a tradition that no one sits above except ה׳. So he reasoned that מיטטרון might be a second power. This is the wrong thought the פסוק in step 12 warned about.

keyTerms.meaning: The name of a high angel.
Two powers, the heresy that there is another ruling force besides ה׳.

steps.confusionAlert: 'Heaven forbid' is not part of אחר's thought. The גמרא adds it to distance itself from the idea of two powers.

phrases.english: He saw Mitatron
who had been given permission
to sit and write the merits of Israel.
He said: We have a tradition
that above there is
no sitting and no competition,
no back of the neck and no tiredness.
phrases.notes: 'No back of the neck' means no one up there turns their back to ה׳; everyone faces Him.

phrases.english: Perhaps, Heaven forbid,
there are two powers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Seeing מיטטרון sitting, which went against the tradition that no one sits above, led אחר to think there might be two powers.

steps.title: מיטטרון is punished, then allowed to erase אחר's merits
steps.stepSummary: מיטטרון was struck with sixty fiery lashes for not standing when אחר saw him. He was then allowed to erase אחר's merits.
steps.simpleTranslation: They took מיטטרון out and struck him with sixty lashes of fire. They said to him: Why didn't you stand up when you saw him? He was then given permission to erase the merits of אחר.
steps.whatsHappening: Heaven punishes מיטטרון for staying seated in front of אחר, since that caused the mistake. Then מיטטרון is given permission to erase אחר's merits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Standing up would have shown that מיטטרון is only a servant, and the mistake would not have happened. Being struck also showed clearly that he is not a power. Since he was hurt because of אחר, he was allowed to wipe out אחר's merits.

phrases.english: They took Mitatron out
and struck him sixty lashes of fire.
They said to him:
What is the reason that when you saw him
you did not stand up before him?
phrases.notes: 'Him' is אחר. מיטטרון should have stood so no one would mistake him for a ruler.

phrases.english: He was given permission
to erase the merits of Acher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: the result of אחר's mistake.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מיטטרון was punished to show he is not a power, and was allowed to erase אחר's merits.

steps.title: A בת קול shuts אחר out
steps.stepSummary: A בת קול calls everyone to return, except אחר.
steps.simpleTranslation: A heavenly voice went out and said: 'Return, wayward children,' except for אחר.
steps.whatsHappening: A voice from heaven calls the Jewish people back to ה׳ but leaves out אחר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק invites everyone to do תשובה, but the בת קול adds an exception. This sets up אחר's reaction in the next step.

phrases.english: A heavenly voice went out and said:
"Return, wayward children"
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 3:22

phrases.english: except for Acher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: the heavenly result for אחר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone is called to תשובה except אחר.

steps.title: אחר decides to enjoy this world
steps.stepSummary: Believing he has lost the next world, אחר decides to enjoy this one and goes off to evil ways.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Since that man has been driven out of that world, let him go out and enjoy this world. אחר went out to evil ways.
steps.whatsHappening: אחר hears that he is shut out and decides there is no point in keeping the Torah, so he abandons it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reasoning is: no reward is waiting, so he might as well take pleasure now. Despair, not just doubt, pushes him to leave completely.

keyTerms.meaning: That world, meaning the World to Come.
Evil ways, a bad way of life.

phrases.english: He said: Since has been driven out
that man from that world,
phrases.notes: 'That man' is how he talks about himself. 'That world' is the World to Come.

phrases.english: let him go out and enjoy this world.
Acher went out to evil ways.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר: הוֹאִיל וְאִיטְּרִיד הָהוּא גַּבְרָא מֵהָהוּא עָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: אחר's reaction to the בת קול.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אחר gave up on the next world and abandoned the Torah.

steps.title: How אלישע בן אבויה got the name אחר
steps.stepSummary: A prostitute recognizes אלישע בן אבויה. He openly breaks שבת in front of her, and she says he is 'someone else.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He went out, found a prostitute, and propositioned her. She said to him: Aren't you אלישע בן אבויה? He uprooted a radish from a patch on שבת and gave it to her. She said: He is someone else.
steps.whatsHappening: This story shows how far אחר fell and explains where his name comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She cannot believe that the great אלישע בן אבויה would do this. By breaking שבת in front of her, he shows he no longer keeps the Torah. Her words 'he is someone else' become his name, אחר.

keyTerms.meaning: The real name of the תנא known as אחר.

steps.whatToRemember: אחר is אלישע בן אבויה. He was called 'the other one' because after leaving the Torah he was no longer the same person.

phrases.english: He went out, found a prostitute, and propositioned her.
She said to him:
Aren't you Elisha ben Avuya?
He uprooted a radish from a patch on Shabbat
and gave it to her.
She said: He is someone else.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a concrete example of the 'evil ways' from step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אחר openly broke שבת and was called 'the other one.'

steps.title: אחר asks רבי מאיר about a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: After going astray, אחר asks his student רבי מאיר what the פסוק 'This one opposite that one God made' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: אחר asked רבי מאיר, after he had gone astray: What is the meaning of what is written, 'God made this one opposite that one'?
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins. אחר asks רבי מאיר to explain a פסוק from קהלת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after leaving the Torah, אחר still discusses פסוקים with רבי מאיר. The question sets up a back-and-forth about what the פסוק means.

phrases.english: Acher asked Rabbi Meir
after he had gone out to evil ways,
he said to him: What is it that is written:
"Also this one opposite that one
God has made"?
phrases.notes: קהלת 7:14

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about אחר after his fall.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'גם את זה לעומת זה עשה האלהים.'

steps.title: רבי מאיר: everything was created with a counterpart
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר explains that for everything ה׳ created, He created a matching counterpart, like mountains and hills or seas and rivers.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Everything the הקדוש ברוך הוא created, He created something corresponding to it. He created mountains, He created hills. He created seas, He created rivers.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר answers with a simple explanation: creation comes in matching pairs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר reads 'this opposite that' as a big thing paired with a smaller thing of the same kind. His examples come from nature, which leaves room for אחר to push back with a deeper reading.

phrases.english: He said to him: Everything that created
the Holy One, Blessed be He, He created its counterpart.
He created mountains, He created hills;
He created seas, He created rivers.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: כׇּל מַה שֶּׁבָּרָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, בָּרָא כְּנֶגְדּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אחר's question from step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Every creation has a matching counterpart: mountains and hills, seas and rivers.

steps.title: Everyone has a portion in both גן עדן and גיהנם
steps.stepSummary: אחר rejects רבי מאיר's explanation of 'this opposite that' and quotes רבי עקיבא‎: ה׳ created צדיקים and רשעים, גן עדן and גיהנם, and each person has a portion in both.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Your teacher רבי עקיבא did not explain it that way. He said that ה׳ created righteous people and wicked people, and He created גן עדן and גיהנם. Every person has two portions, one in גן עדן and one in גיהנם. If a person earns it and becomes righteous, he takes his own portion and his friend's portion in גן עדן. If a person is found guilty and becomes wicked, he takes his own portion and his friend's portion in גיהנם.
steps.whatsHappening: אחר pushes aside רבי מאיר's 'mountains and hills' answer and gives רבי עקיבא's deeper explanation of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר read 'this opposite that' as talking about nature, like mountains matching hills. אחר says רבי עקיבא read it as talking about people and their reward: צדיקים match רשעים, and גן עדן matches גיהנם. Each person ends up with a double share in the place he earns.

keyTerms.meaning: The Garden of Eden, the place of reward

steps.confusionAlert: 'He takes his friend's portion' does not mean he is stealing it. The friend gave up his own spot in that place by the choices he made, so that empty share goes to someone else.

phrases.english: He said to him: Rabbi Akiva, your teacher,
phrases.notes: The speaker here is אחר, answering רבי מאיר's explanation from the step before.

phrases.english: did not say so, but rather:
He created the righteous, He created the wicked;
He created Gan Eden, He created Gehinnom.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד יֵשׁ לוֹ שְׁנֵי חֲלָקִים,
phrases.english: Each and every person has two portions,
one in Gan Eden and one in Gehinnom.
If he merits and is righteous, he takes his portion
and his friend's portion in Gan Eden;
if he is found guilty and is wicked, he takes his portion
and his friend's portion in Gehinnom.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא רַבְּךָ לֹא אָמַר כָּךְ, אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבי מאיר's nature-based reading in step 20 with רבי עקיבא's reading about reward and punishment.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי מאיר's explanation of the פסוק 'זה לעומת זה'
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It reads the פסוק as being about nature, while רבי עקיבא read it as being about צדיקים and רשעים and their portions.

steps.title: The verses that show a double portion
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא gives the source for the double portion: about צדיקים it says 'they shall inherit double', and about רשעים it says 'double destruction'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said: What is the פסוק that teaches this? About the righteous it is written: 'Therefore in their land they shall inherit double.' About the wicked it is written: 'And destroy them with double destruction.'
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא steps in and shows where in תנ״ך we see that each person gets a double share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's idea that everyone takes two portions needed a source. The word 'מִשְׁנֶה' (double) appears both for reward and for punishment. That matches the two-portion picture exactly.

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiya said: What is the verse for this?
About the righteous it is written:
"Therefore in their land they shall inherit double";
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 61:7

phrases.english: about the wicked it is written:
"And destroy them with double destruction."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 17:18

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source verses for רבי עקיבא's teaching in step 21.
steps.raayaObject: Each person receives a double portion, in גן עדן or in גיהנם
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו 61:7 and ירמיהו 17:18, which both use the word מִשְׁנֶה

steps.title: אחר asks about gold and glass
steps.stepSummary: After going astray, אחר asks רבי מאיר what the פסוק in איוב means when it compares something to gold and glass.
steps.simpleTranslation: אחר asked רבי מאיר, after he had gone off to evil ways: What does the פסוק mean, 'Gold and glass cannot equal it, and vessels of fine gold cannot be traded for it'?
steps.whatsHappening: A new conversation begins. אחר asks רבי מאיר to explain a פסוק, which sets up the next exchange.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The puzzle is why glass is mentioned next to gold, since glass is cheap. The answer will need to explain what gold and glass have in common.

keyTerms.meaning: Evil ways, a bad way of life
Can equal it, can be compared to it

phrases.english: Aher asked Rabbi Meir
after he had gone out to evil ways:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"Gold and glass cannot equal it,
nor can vessels of fine gold be its exchange"?
phrases.notes: איוב 28:17. The פסוק is talking about wisdom.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאַל אַחֵר אֶת רַבִּי מֵאִיר לְאַחַר שֶׁיָּצָא לְתַרְבּוּת רָעָה, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the same pattern as step 19, with a new פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the comparison of the Torah to gold and glass in איוב 28:17 means

steps.title: Torah is hard to gain and easy to lose
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר explains that Torah is as hard to acquire as gold, and as easy to lose as glass is to break.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is talking about words of Torah. They are as hard to acquire as gold vessels and vessels of fine gold, and as easy to lose as glass vessels.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר answers by explaining what gold and glass each teach about Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gold is rare and expensive, so it stands for how hard Torah is to get. Glass breaks easily, so it stands for how quickly Torah can be forgotten.

phrases.english: He said to him: These are words of Torah,
which are hard to acquire
like gold vessels and vessels of fine gold,
and easy to lose like glass vessels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Gold shows that Torah is hard to acquire; glass shows that Torah is easy to lose.

steps.title: Broken vessels can be fixed, and so can a sinning scholar
steps.stepSummary: אחר again quotes רבי עקיבא: just as broken gold and glass vessels can be repaired, a תלמיד חכם who sinned can also be repaired.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Your teacher רבי עקיבא did not explain it that way. He said: Gold vessels and glass vessels can be fixed even after they break. In the same way, a תלמיד חכם can be fixed even after he sins.
steps.whatsHappening: אחר rejects רבי מאיר's reading and gives רבי עקיבא's reading, which focuses on what gold and glass have in common.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר contrasted gold and glass. רבי עקיבא found what they share: both can be melted down and remade after breaking. That becomes a message of hope that a sinning תלמיד חכם can always be repaired.

keyTerms.meaning: A remedy, a way to be fixed

steps.whyThisMatters: אחר himself is quoting the very teaching that should give him hope, and this sets up רבי מאיר's plea in the next step.

phrases.english: He said to him: Rabbi Akiva, your teacher,
did not say so, but rather:
Just as gold vessels and glass vessels,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנִּשְׁבְּרוּ — יֵשׁ לָהֶם תַּקָּנָה,
phrases.english: even though they broke, have a remedy,
so too a Torah scholar,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁסָּרַח — יֵשׁ לוֹ תַּקָּנָה.
phrases.english: even though he sinned, has a remedy.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא רַבָּךְ לֹא אָמַר כָּךְ, אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי מאיר's reading in step 24, the same way step 21 rejected step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי מאיר's reading of the gold and glass פסוק
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It focuses on how gold and glass differ, while רבי עקיבא focused on what they share: both can be repaired.

steps.title: רבי מאיר pleads: then you come back too
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר uses אחר's own words against him: if a sinning תלמיד חכם can be fixed, then you should return as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Then you too, come back!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר turns אחר's teaching into a personal challenge and begs him to do תשובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אחר just said that a sinning תלמיד חכם has a remedy. If that is true, nothing should stop אחר himself from returning. This is both a challenge and a heartfelt plea.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: אַף אַתָּה חֲזוֹר בָּךְ!
phrases.english: He said to him: You too, return!
phrases.notes: Now רבי מאיר is the one speaking, using אחר's own teaching.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the teaching of step 25 to אחר himself.
steps.kashyaTarget: אחר's choice to stay in his evil ways
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By his own teaching, a sinning תלמיד חכם has a remedy, so he should return.

steps.title: אחר answers: I was excluded
steps.stepSummary: אחר answers that he already heard from behind the heavenly curtain that everyone is called to return, except אחר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I already heard from behind the curtain: 'Return, wayward children', except for אחר.
steps.whatsHappening: אחר explains why he will not come back. He believes Heaven itself has shut him out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This repeats the בת קול from step 16 as אחר's personal reason. The general rule that a scholar can be fixed does not help him, because he believes he was named as the one exception.
steps.whatToRemember: אחר knew and taught that every sinner can return, yet he felt the heavenly voice had shut the door on him alone.

phrases.english: He said to him: I have already heard
from behind the curtain:
phrases.notes: This is the heavenly voice from step 16.

phrases.english: "Return, wayward children,"
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 3:22

phrases.english: except for Aher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי מאיר's plea in step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The heavenly voice called everyone back except אחר.

steps.title: אחר rides on שבת and warns רבי מאיר about the boundary
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells of אחר riding a horse on שבת while רבי מאיר walked behind him to learn Torah. אחר warns him to turn back because they reached the תחום שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: There once was a story with אחר, who was riding a horse on שבת. רבי מאיר was walking behind him to learn Torah from him. אחר said to him: Meir, turn back, because I have already measured by my horse's steps that the תחום שבת ends here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related story about the two of them. This sets up the same plea and answer that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אחר himself is breaking שבת, yet he still carefully measures the boundary so that his student does not sin. His Torah knowledge is still sharp even while he lives far from it.

keyTerms.meaning: The שבת boundary, the limit for walking on שבת

steps.whyThisMatters: 'Turn back' (חֲזוֹר לְאַחֲרֶיךָ) sets up רבי מאיר's reply, which uses the same word חֲזוֹר in the sense of returning to ה׳.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: There was an incident with Aher
who was riding on a horse on Shabbat,
and Rabbi Meir was walking behind him
to learn Torah from his mouth.
He said to him: Meir, turn back,
for I have already measured by my horse's steps
that the Shabbat boundary is up to here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new story that repeats the theme of steps 26 and 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אחר, while breaking שבת himself, warns רבי מאיר not to walk past the תחום שבת.

steps.title: רבי מאיר pleads again
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר turns אחר's words around: just as you tell me to turn back, you too should turn back to ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You too, turn back.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר uses אחר's warning as a chance to beg him once more to do תשובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אחר told him to turn back physically at the boundary. רבי מאיר answers that אחר should turn back spiritually. The same word is used both ways.

keyTerms.meaning: Turn back, which here also means do תשובה

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: אַף אַתָּה חֲזוֹר בָּךְ.
phrases.english: He said to him: You too, return.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns אחר's 'turn back' from step 28 into a call for תשובה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: You tell me to turn back from a sin, so you should turn back from yours.

steps.title: אחר repeats: I am the exception
steps.stepSummary: אחר reminds רבי מאיר that he already told him about the heavenly voice that excluded him from returning.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Didn't I already tell you that I heard from behind the curtain: 'Return, wayward children', except for אחר?
steps.whatsHappening: אחר gives the same answer as before and closes the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story ends the same way as the earlier conversation. רבי מאיר keeps reaching out, and אחר keeps pointing to the heavenly voice as the reason he cannot come back.
steps.whatToRemember: Both stories end the same way. רבי מאיר keeps calling his teacher to return, and אחר keeps answering that the heavenly voice excluded him.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: וְלֹא כְּבָר אָמַרְתִּי לְךָ
phrases.english: He said to him: Have I not already told you
that I already heard from behind the curtain:
"Return, wayward children," except for Aher?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the plea in step 29 with the same answer as step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The heavenly voice already excluded אחר from the call to return.

steps.title: The first child's verse: no peace for the wicked
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר takes אחר into a בית מדרש. אחר asks a child for his verse, and the child answers 'There is no peace, said ה׳, for the wicked.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He took hold of him and brought him into the study hall. He said to a child: 'Tell me your verse.' The child said: 'There is no peace, said ה׳, for the wicked.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר physically brings אחר into a בית מדרש, still hoping he will do תשובה. אחר asks a child what פסוק he learned, and the answer sounds like bad news for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אחר has just said he is shut out from returning, but רבי מאיר keeps trying anyway. Asking a child for his verse works like a sign from Heaven. The verse the child gives, 'no peace for the wicked,' seems to back up what אחר already believes about himself.

keyTerms.meaning: He took hold of him / pressed him
Recite your verse to me (the verse you learned today)

steps.confusionAlert: The person asking the child is אחר, not רבי מאיר. רבי מאיר is the one doing the bringing; אחר is the one asking the children.

phrases.english: He took hold of him and brought him into the study hall.
phrases.notes: Even after hearing about the heavenly voice, רבי מאיר is the one dragging אחר in.

phrases.english: He said to a child:
phrases.notes: Here it is אחר who speaks to the child.

phrases.english: Recite your verse to me.
phrases.notes: He is asking for the verse the child learned that day, as a kind of sign about himself.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: ״אֵין שָׁלוֹם אָמַר ה׳ לָרְשָׁעִים״.
phrases.english: He said to him: "There is no peace, said ה׳, for the wicked."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 48:22

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After אחר again says he is shut out, רבי מאיר tries a new approach and brings him into a בית מדרש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first child's verse, 'There is no peace for the wicked,' seems to confirm that אחר is shut out.

steps.title: The second child's verse: sin that cannot be washed away
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר brings אחר to another place. A second child recites a verse saying that even with niter and soap, the sin stays marked before ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: He brought him to another synagogue. He said to a child: 'Tell me your verse.' The child said: 'Even if you wash with niter and use a lot of soap, your sin is still marked before Me.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר tries again in a second place, and אחר again asks a child for his verse. This child's verse also sounds harsh, saying sin cannot simply be scrubbed off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern repeats on purpose: a new place, the same question, and another discouraging answer. This verse adds a sharper idea than the first one. Even strong efforts to 'clean' oneself seem not to remove the stain, which matches אחר's belief that his תשובה would not work.

phrases.english: He brought him to another synagogue.
He said to a child:
Recite your verse to me.
He said to him: "For though you wash with niter,
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 2:22

phrases.english: and use much soap,
your sin is still marked before Me."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This repeats the same test in a second place and gets a second discouraging verse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The second child's verse says sin stays marked even after much washing, which again seems to confirm אחר's view.

steps.title: A third try begins
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר brings אחר to a third synagogue, and אחר starts to ask again. The story continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: He brought him to yet another synagogue. He said to him...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is starting the third round of the same test, and the child's answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is decided here yet. The repeated wording tells us the same pattern is going on: a new place, the same question to a child. It builds tension toward the third verse.

phrases.english: He brought him to another synagogue.
He said to...
phrases.notes: The sentence keeps going on the next amud, where אחר asks the next child.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַיְּילֵיהּ לְבֵי כְּנִישְׁתָּא אַחֲרִיתִי, אֲמַר לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This starts a third round of the same test after two discouraging verses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup only: a third place is visited, and the child's verse follows on the next amud.
